To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the solubility, density, viscosity of the mixture of R- 600a and POE oil were determined experimentally and the experimental data was correlated with the Hei–Prausnite and Flory– Huggins activity models.

the solubility of R-600 in the polyol ester is high, that the density and viscosity are well predicted by the Peng–Robison EoS and by a first-order Redlick-Kister and Grunberg–Nissan model, respectively.
the Heil–Prasunitz model and the Peng–Rubinson equation of state are suitable for correlating the solubility of R-600 in a POE ISO-7 lubricant oil.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and application of thermodynamic, transport, and phase equilibrium models in the context of a new refrigerant, R-600a, and its mixtures with polyol ester oils.
the thermodynamic and transport properties of a R-600a–lubricant mixture.
the development and application of a novel experimental facility for measuring the physical properties of mixtures of low GWP refrigerants with lubricating oils.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the experimental data and the correlations are consistent and the models used are suitable for practical applications.
the experimental data presented here can be used to validate and improve the existing models for the prediction of the solubility and physical properties of mixtures of R-600 and polyol esters.
the models are adequate for the description of the physical properties of R-600 + POE ISO 7.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Peng–Robenson EoS and the Redlich–Kisster model are the best for the VLE and liquid density, while the Grunberg–Nissan model is the best for the prediction of viscosity.
the experimental data are well correlated with models, which is an important step towards the development of reliable thermophysical models.

the Heil–Prusnitz and Peng–Robinson activity models, Peng–Robinson density model and the Eyring liquid model are recommended for the design of refrigeration systems operating with R-600a + POE ISO 7 mixtures at temperatures up to 60 ° Solubility, viscosity, and density of a mixture of 2-chloro-1,1,1,2-tetrafluoroethane (R-124)
The main takeaway from our work is that
the experimental data on the physical properties of the R-600a + POE ISO 7 system can serve as reference data for the development of models and correlations for refrigerant–oil systems.

the VLE, liquid density and viscosity data can be predicted using simple models and that the experimental data can be used to develop a predictive model for the solubility of R-600 in lubricating oils.
the experimental VLE, density, and viscosity data are useful for developing and testing thermodynamic models and viscosity correlations.
